subject: environmental-science
title: ITQs and the Common Fisheries Policy
welcome_lead: Property rights, quotas and the EU's struggle to share a shrinking sea.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on individual transferable quotas and CFP reform.
final_note: Property rights can rebuild stocks — or concentrate fishing in a few hands.

concepts.def: Fishing right allocated to vessels, tradable on a quota market.
EU framework governing fisheries since 1983; reformed 2013.
2013 CFP rule to land all catches, ending discards of quota species.
Target reference point in reformed CFP since 2015.
Operation where multiple stocks are caught together — complicates TAC setting.
World's most studied ITQ, introduced 1984 — credited with stock recovery.

walkthroughs.body_html: ITQs give long-term security, incentivising stewardship. Iceland and New Zealand pioneer cases.
The 2013 reform required MSY targets and ended discards, but enforcement remains uneven.
ITQ markets concentrate quota in larger vessels, displacing small-scale fishers. Caps and community quotas attempt to balance.

mcqs.q: ITQ systems are typically credited with:
options: Aligning long-term stewardship with property rights
Landing all catches of quota species
